trials.notes: Used the correct `WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment()` path for BODY-fragment, tree-aware table traversal. All processor methods used are documented, and execution had no `_doing_it_wrong` records. The walk is idiomatic: first `TABLE`, record depth, single `next_token()` loop, collect only `#text` via `get_modifiable_text()`, and rely on virtual closers. Minor issue: it trims cell text, while the API/text-content contract preserves decoded text as returned.

Correct processor choice and fully documented API usage. The implementation follows the rendered guidance closely: a single depth-bounded token walk, explicit row/cell state, `#text` gating before `get_modifiable_text()`, and no nested cursor loops. It also preserves whitespace and flushes partial state defensively.

Correctly uses `WP_HTML_Processor` and only documented methods. The solution follows the intended one-pass state-machine pattern and uses decoded `#text` tokens only. It has a small amount of dead state (`$current_cell_depth`) and a redundant final flush, but no API misuse and no hidden-test failures.

failure_analysis: No hidden case failed in these trials: all three passed 8/8 cases, and every case reported empty `_doing_it_wrong` records. The docs did well on the central risks for this task: the Tag Processor overview says structure-aware work and text-content extraction belong to `WP_HTML_Processor`; the HTML Processor `next_token()` section explains single-cursor walking, virtual closers for implicit/end-of-input closures, synthesized table structure, and depth-bounded loops; `get_current_depth()` explains why `>=` is the right subtree guard; and `get_modifiable_text()` explains decoded text and why callers should only read it after checking `get_token_type() === '#text'` for ordinary DOM-style text. The main near-miss was trial 1 adding `trim()`, which would lose significant leading/trailing text even though the API returns decoded text without whitespace normalization. All candidates also treated incomplete input as best-effort extraction, which is consistent with the docs' read-only caller-policy language for this task.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs say returned text is decoded, but they do not explicitly say that leading/trailing whitespace is preserved and should not be normalized for text-content extraction unless the caller contract says so.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a sentence to the text-extraction recipe: concatenate the returned `#text` strings exactly as returned; do not `trim()`, collapse whitespace, or re-escape unless the caller explicitly asks for normalized text.

doc_gaps.problem: The existing single-loop example is one repeated level (`DT`). The table task required nested repeated regions (rows containing cells), and models succeeded, but a general nested-state example would make the pattern more transferable.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a general example or note showing two independent state variables for nested repeated regions, such as groups/items, without making it table-specific.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs mention checking `get_last_error()` and `paused_at_incomplete_token()`, but the policy distinction between best-effort read-only extraction and strict complete-input extraction is spread across sections.
doc_gaps.suggestion: In the factory or token-walk docs, add a compact decision rule: read-only extractors may return accumulated data after virtual closers; strict consumers should drain/check `paused_at_incomplete_token()` and `get_last_error()` before trusting completeness.
